thread.title: Samsung’s Full-Screen Patent Could Take ‘Galaxy,’ ‘Note’ to New Extremes

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Samsung’s Full-Screen Patent Could Take ‘Galaxy,’ ‘Note’ to New Extremes
text:
Drawing from a Samsung patent application for a "fullscreen" device that could be a future "Galaxy" smartphone or "Note" phablet from the company. Samsung Electronics (005930KS) spent 2017 leading Apple ( AAPL ) in nearly bezel-less screens, where glass covers almost all of the face of the device, with little frame to interfere.
There was the " Galaxy S8 ” in March , and the gorgeous “ Note 8 ” phablet in August really improved further upon that display magic.
From our friends in the Netherlands, LetsGoDigital , came word late yesterday of a new patent application with the World Intellectual Property Organization, for something that is supposed to be an “electronic apparatus employing full front screen,” which seems basically like a device with no bezel whatsoever.
The device also has several ways to bury a fingerprint sensor underneath the cover glass and OLED display and touch sensor, via a kind of tunneling through several layers and uses of reflected light, which would get rid of the awkwardness of fingerprint sensors on the back.
LetsGoDigital’s Ilse Jurrien writes that there’s so much out there about the expected " Galaxy S9 ” — the follow-on to the S8 that most believe will arrive with Samsung's customary “ Unpacked ” event in Barcelona later this month — that this full-screen device won’t be the 9.
Rather, Jurrien thinks this design might end up being the “Note 9” or next year’s “Galaxy S10."
At any rate, the patent application, which you can download from the WIPO’s Web site , is in Korean, but a rough translation via Google Translate reveals some fascinating qualities that go beyond just having a big screen.
Samsung is innovating with touch as well. It proposes over-loading each icon on the screen with multiple functions. So, for example, pressing the traditional “home” icon, which is now no longer a button but just an icon, can start up the camera or a voice recorder , just by a user varying the amount of pressure exerted by a user when they press with their finger.
It’s kind of an expansion of the “Force Touch” approach Apple pioneered with the iPhone, but taken to greater lengths.
Samsung shares on Friday traded down by about 3% to ₩2,235,000.
